title: Land Cruiser J20 / J25 (FJ25)
verdict: The FJ25 is the Land Cruiser before anyone knew what a Land Cruiser was: one gear in the transfer case, drums at every corner and a 3.9-litre six that Toyota sold against the Jeep on horsepower alone. Only about 220 Land Cruisers reached America from 1958 to 1960, and the survivors are worth more as history than as trail rigs.

paragraphs: The 20 Series is where the Land Cruiser stopped being a police jeep and became a product. Toyota had renamed its BJ 'Jeep' the Land Cruiser in June 1954, after Willys objected to the use of its trademark, and the second-generation truck that followed in 1955 was redesigned for civilian buyers. Toyota's own lineage pages date the launch to November 1955 (its UK history says August). It got rounder bodywork, a roomier cabin and, within months, the 3.9-litre F straight-six. The short-wheelbase FJ25 is the one everyone remembers, but the family also included the longer FJ28, early B-engined BJ trucks and a run of vans and fire engines.

story.heading: FROM POLICE JEEP TO EXPORT HERO
paragraphs: The name came first. Wikipedia quotes technical director Hanji Umehara explaining that Toyota's real rival in export markets was Land Rover, so the new name had to sound no less dignified than 'Land Rover.' Toyota's UK history says the first export shipment went to Pakistan in 1954 and Saudi Arabia followed in 1955. That makes the J20 the first Land Cruiser built with export in mind: Toyota says the 20 Series was the generation that began shipping to North America and other overseas markets in large volume. It came with export suspension uprated over the Japanese spec, because, as Toyota UK puts it, Japan had no highways at the time.

Toyota's 75-year history tracks the numbers. Land Cruiser exports went from 98 in 1955 to 518 in 1956, then jumped to 2,502 in 1957, when Toyota tried to make up for weak domestic sales overseas. Venezuela took 52 in autumn 1956 and 795 in 1957 for oilfields and cattle ranches. Burma got 22 in July 1956 as war reparations, and Australia got a dozen in August 1957. Toyota UK adds that after US military trials in 1957, Land Cruisers made up 38.2 percent of all vehicles exported from Japan that year, across every brand. The cheap little Toyota had become Japan's most important export.

story.heading: THE F ENGINE AND A VERY SIMPLE DRIVELINE
paragraphs: At launch the J20 offered two petrol sixes: the 3.4-litre B from the BJ and the 3.9-litre F, which had previously been used only in the fire-engine chassis. Toyota says the range was cut to the F alone in mid-1956. Toyota's lineage page rates the FJ25's F at 105 PS (net) at 3,200 rpm. A period US dealer checklist posted on IH8MUD pitched the FJ25 against the [[jeep/cj-5|CJ-5]] as having 'almost twice the horsepower at no extra cost.' Wikipedia says the engine was also moved 120 mm forward to free up cabin space, and that the ride improved with longer leaf springs adapted from Toyota's light truck.

The rest is crude by modern standards. Toyota describes the four-wheel-drive J20 as having a one-speed transfer case: no low range, which didn't arrive until the [[land-cruiser/fj40|FJ40]] in 1960. A four-speed floor-shift manual (as listed by Bring a Trailer, RM Sotheby's and Barrett-Jackson for surviving trucks) did the work instead. Toyota also built a rear-drive version for police patrol work. Wheelbases were 2,285 mm (FJ25) and 2,430 mm (the longer FJ28), with a 2,650 mm chassis added near the end in 1959. Brakes were drums all round.

story.heading: AMERICA, AUSTRALIA AND BRAZIL
paragraphs: America came late and slowly. Autoblog's visit to the Land Cruiser Heritage Museum describes the first Land Cruiser sold in the US: a 1958 FJ25 ordered by Rose Toyota and delivered at the port, because the dealership wasn't finished yet, to a Long Beach schoolteacher. It was the only Land Cruiser Toyota sold in America that year, alongside 287 Toyopet Crowns. The import figures compiled in IH8MUD's FJ2X registry show 61 Land Cruisers in 1959 and 162 in 1960.

Australia was a bigger deal. Wikipedia credits B&D Motors with importing FJ25/28 cab-chassis trucks from 1959 and says the Land Cruiser was the first Japanese vehicle regularly exported to Australia. A handful went to work for Thiess on the Snowy Mountains Scheme. In Brazil, Toyota began building the FJ25L in São Bernardo in May 1959. Its 75-year history calls this its first full-fledged overseas knockdown production. Brazil switched to Mercedes-Benz diesels and the Bandeirante name in 1962 and kept building the 25-based truck until 1968. Japan replaced the J20 with the [[land-cruiser/fj40|40 Series]] in 1960.

story.heading: THE COLLECTOR'S TRUCK
paragraphs: Today the FJ25 is a collector's piece first and an off-roader a distant second. IH8MUD's FJ25 Owners Group runs a worldwide count of surviving 20 Series trucks and a VIN registry, and warns about 'Frankencruisers': FJ40 tubs wearing an FJ25 frame number. Most of the FJ25s sold on Bring a Trailer since 2019 were restored in Colombia or Costa Rica and imported later. On Bring a Trailer, FJ25s sold for $14,001 to $39,000 between 2019 and 2026, and RM Sotheby's got $70,000 for a restored 1960 soft-top in 2019.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE NAME
callout.title: Why it isn't called a Jeep
paragraphs: Toyota's prototype of 1951 was literally the 'Toyota Jeep BJ', named for its B engine and the American vehicle it imitated. Toyota says the National Police Reserve preferred Mitsubishi's licence-built Willys, so the BJ went into civilian production in 1953. It was renamed in June 1954 because 'Jeep' was a Willys-Overland trademark.

Umehara's reasoning, as Wikipedia quotes him, was aimed at Britain rather than America: 'In England we had another competitor – Land Rover.' The name had already been used on a Studebaker, which ended production the same year. The J20 was the first truck designed from the start to wear it, and the first to carry it abroad in numbers. The [[land-rover/series|Series Land Rover]] it was named against is still its natural rival in a vintage line-up.

engineering_intro: The J20 is a 1950s utility truck in its purest form: a ladder frame, leaf springs on solid axles, a big slow-revving six and a transfer case that only connects the front axle. Many engine parts are shared with early FJ40s, but the chassis, body and much of the trim are unique, which is why surviving FJ25 owners trade parts among themselves rather than at the parts counter.

engineering.note: A 2,650 mm chassis was added in 1959, the basis for the rare four-door FJ35V van.

engineering.v: Solid axles, leaf springs front and rear
engineering.note: Longer springs than the BJ; IH8MUD members say the FJ25's rear springs and spring hangers are unique, while the fronts match the 40.
No low range. A two-wheel-drive police version was also built.
105 PS net at 3,200 rpm (Toyota). Early trucks could have the 3.4 L B six until mid-1956.
Low first gear does the work that a low-range transfer case would do on later trucks.
IH8MUD: both shoes are identical (no leading/trailing), set with cam adjusters; 1-inch wheel-cylinder cups.

generations_table.note: Carried over from the BJ; Toyota dropped it from the J20 range in mid-1956.
2,285 mm wheelbase; soft-top, hardtop and pickup bodies. The truck most collectors mean by 'FJ25.'
2,430 mm wheelbase; pickups, vans and the very rare FJ28L survivors.
Four-door Gifu-bodied van on the 2,650 mm J20 chassis, built for nine months; Wikipedia says about 60 were made.
Toyota do Brasil's first local build, from May 1959.
Brazilian 25-based trucks with Mercedes diesels, built until August 1968.

buying_checks.head: Prove it's really a 25
buying_checks.body: IH8MUD's FJ25 group has seen FJ40 tubs on rebuilt frames wearing FJ25 VIN plates. Real FJ25 tells include the fuel tank under the seat, round rear wheel cut-outs, a flat floor with no hump for an offset transfer case, a centered rear differential and an FJ25-specific steering center link. Photograph the frame from underneath, especially the crossmembers and spring hangers, before you pay a 25 price.

buying_checks.head: Match the numbers
buying_checks.body: The data plate lists frame and engine numbers, and FJ25 VINs read like 9FJ25-12645L (year digit, model, serial, L for left-hand drive). Registry members note engines weren't installed in strict numerical order, but the block number should sit in the right range for the frame. Check the block stamping against the plate; Bring a Trailer listings photograph both.

buying_checks.head: Know where it was restored
buying_checks.body: Most FJ25s sold in the US recently were refurbished in Colombia, Costa Rica or elsewhere in Latin America and then imported. That's fine, but restoration quality varies. Look for cracked paint at panel joints, swapped seats and later running gear. Get the title and import paperwork in order before you pay.

buying_checks.head: Original engine or a 2F?
buying_checks.body: Swaps are common, and the market notices. In June 2025 a 2F-powered 1959 FJ25 sold on Bring a Trailer for $14,250. In July 2026 a refurbished F-powered 1959 sold there for $37,500. A later 2F head on an F block is a 'Frankencruiser' sign that IH8MUD members flag.

buying_checks.head: Wheels and FJ25-only parts
buying_checks.body: FJ25 wheels are scarce. IH8MUD members report that 15-inch disc-brake wheels hit the tie-rod ends, 15-inch drum wheels won't clear the FJ25's drum rivets, and most other 16-inch wheels have too small a center bore. Rear spring hangers and bolts, top bows and the pre-1960 toolbox lid (diagonal ribs, five catches) are FJ25-specific, so missing pieces are expensive to find.

buying_checks.head: Brakes and hydraulics
buying_checks.body: Specter Off-Road lists its FJ25 brake and clutch master-cylinder kits (1-inch bore, cast iron) as discontinued, so check that the hydraulics work before you buy. Some restored trucks have front disc conversions, which make them safer but less original.

buying_checks.head: Year details matter to purists
buying_checks.body: Owners report that 1958-and-earlier trucks (and some 1959s) use a three-bolt front-fender-to-frame pattern, that the 1959 wears the 'Thunderbird' emblem rather than the oval, and that the cradle-style front engine mount and the old toolbox lid both changed around 1960. If you're paying for originality, get the details checked by someone from the owners' group.

repairs.title: Drum brake reline and adjustment
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day for all four wheels
repairs.symptoms: Pulling, a long pedal or brakes that need pumping, on a truck with four drums and no booster.
repairs.fix: Following an IH8MUD FJ25 Owners Group walkthrough: strip each backing plate and set all adjusters to minimum before fitting new shoes. The upper adjuster turns 270 degrees from its flat side and the lower one 180 degrees, with a notch visible from the back. Both shoes are identical, with no leading or trailing shoe. Lube the shoe contact points and the felt washer under the retainer, then fit the horseshoe clip. Hone the wheel cylinders and fit 1-inch cups. Refit the drums and pump the pedal. Then bring each adjuster out until the shoe just drags and back it off slightly: lower adjusters first, then upper.
repairs.tools: Drum and hub tools · channel-lock pliers (horseshoe clips) · wheel-cylinder hone · 1-inch cups (NAPA 1499 per the IH8MUD FJ25 part list) · DOT 3 fluid

parts.name: Brake master cylinders and brake parts by fitment year
Parking brake shoes, FJ40/45/55 1958–80 (confirm FJ25 fit)

repairs.title: Master cylinder rebuild (brake and clutch)
repairs.symptoms: A sinking pedal, fluid at the firewall, or a clutch that won't fully release.
repairs.fix: The FJ25's brake and clutch master cylinders are 1-inch-bore cast-iron units. Specter Off-Road lists its FJ25 kits (014-02-FJ25 brake, 018-02-FJ25 clutch) as discontinued, so look for cups of the same bore or have the bores sleeved by a specialist. Strip, hone and inspect the bore, fit new cups and seals, and check the cap. IH8MUD members found vented caps arrived on early-1960s trucks, and earlier caps may not be vented. Bleed both systems with fresh DOT 3.
repairs.tools: Hone · brake fluid · flare-nut wrenches · bleeder kit

parts.name: FJ25 brake master cylinder kit (014-02-FJ25, listed as discontinued)
FJ25 clutch master cylinder kit (018-02-FJ25, listed as discontinued)

repairs.title: Water pump rebuild
repairs.cost: About $125 for a professional rebuild (IH8MUD member report)
repairs.symptoms: Weeping from the pump weep hole, a growling bearing or wobble at the fan.
repairs.fix: New early pumps are hard to find, so owners rebuild the original. One IH8MUD member found that the early pump bearing (Toyota 90369-30008, cross-referenced as Koyo 885141 / FAG W2503) is the same bearing used in the Willys Jeep pump, and that Jeep rebuild kits (BB707) supply the bearing and seal. Others send pumps to a water-pump rebuilder; one member reported about $125. Fit a new bypass hose while it's apart.
repairs.tools: Puller · press · gasket scraper · Willys-type rebuild kit or professional rebuild

parts.name: Thermostat, OEM/Aisin (1958–92 F-series; confirm FJ25 fit)

repairs.title: Ignition tune-up (points, condenser, short-reach plugs)
repairs.cost: About $24 for a points and condenser combo (Cruiser Corps)
repairs.symptoms: Hard starting, misfire or a rough idle on a truck that hasn't been tuned in years.
repairs.fix: Fit new points and condenser and set the gap. Cruiser Corps gives 0.018 in for its 1958–75 F-engine set. The FJ25 takes short-reach plugs: the IH8MUD FJ25 part list gives Champion J8C, NGK B6S or Nippondenso W14-U. Early distributors use a vacuum advance in which the whole distributor body moves. IH8MUD members found aftermarket Delco units on some trucks and advise against them. Replace the cap and rotor if they're cracked or tracked.
repairs.tools: Feeler gauges · dwell meter or timing light · short-reach plugs

parts.name: Points and condenser combo, F engine 1958–75

repairs.title: Valve adjustment and valve cover reseal
repairs.symptoms: Ticking from the top end, oil weeping down the block, or poor running from tight valves.
repairs.fix: The F engine has adjustable rockers, and the procedure is the same as on an early FJ40. Warm the engine, find tight and loose valves with go/no-go feeler gauges, then shut it off and adjust cylinder by cylinder with the intake just closed. Use the clearances in your manual. Fit a new cork gasket: the IH8MUD FJ25 part list gives Toyota 11253-60010 for the original cover gasket.
repairs.tools: Feeler gauges · 17 mm wrench · screwdriver · new gasket

parts.name: Valve cover gasket, F engine 1958–74 (confirm FJ25 fit)

repairs.title: Radiator re-core or replacement
repairs.cost: One owner was quoted $950 to re-core; members say later OEM radiators cost under $400
repairs.symptoms: Creeping temperature, a weeping core or a radiator a shop refuses to repair.
repairs.fix: Early radiators have horizontal fins and are heavy. One IH8MUD seller found the same radiator part number in Toyota books from 1958 to 1962, so FJ25 and early FJ40 radiators match. Owners report using Cool Cruisers of Texas radiators without problems, and one says new late-model OEM radiators 'fit right in' if originality isn't the goal. The original tanks can also be re-cored. Flush the block, fit a new cap and hoses, and check the fan shroud.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · hose clamps · new radiator cap

parts.name: Four-core radiator, FJ40/45 1958–84 (later style; confirm fit)

repairs.title: Carburetor and fuel-system refresh
repairs.symptoms: Stumbling, rich running or a truck that won't start after sitting.
repairs.fix: One IH8MUD owner got a truck that had sat for 15 years running again by cleaning the carburetor, blowing out the fuel lines and adding fresh fuel. For a full rebuild, the FJ25 part list says an F-engine Keyster kit works, but its main metering rod and jet are wrong for the FJ25. Keep the original jet and rod, or source FJ25-correct ones. Specter Off-Road's 1961–62 kit is discontinued and its 1963–68 kits remain listed. Replace the metal-bowl fuel filter element and check the mechanical pump.
repairs.tools: Carb cleaner · screwdrivers · float gauge · fuel line

parts.name: USA carburetor rebuild kits by year (042-03A)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: There's no forum consensus for the FJ25, and the bigger problem is wheels. Restored trucks on Bring a Trailer have worn 6.00-16 military-style tires, and one 1959 ran 265/75R16 all-terrains on its 16-inch steel wheels. IH8MUD members warn that 15-inch disc-brake wheels hit the FJ25's tie-rod ends and 15-inch drum wheels won't clear the drum rivets. Stay with 16-inch wheels and a period-sized tire unless you want to start modifying the truck.

No. Toyota describes the four-wheel-drive J20 as having a one-speed transfer case. The four-speed manual's low first gear has to do the crawling. Toyota's two-speed transfer case arrived with the 40 Series in 1960.

Usually the 3.9-litre F inline-six, which Toyota rates at 105 PS (net) in the FJ25. Early J20s could also have the 3.4-litre B six carried over from the BJ, but Toyota says the range was cut to the F alone in mid-1956.

faq.q: What's the difference between FJ25, FJ28 and FJ35?
faq.a: The FJ25 is the 2,285 mm short wheelbase. The FJ28 is the longer 2,430 mm version, used for pickups and vans. The FJ35V was a four-door van on the 2,650 mm chassis added in 1959. Wikipedia says the FJ35V was built for only nine months in 1960 and that about 60 were made.

faq.q: How many came to the US?
faq.a: Very few. The first US Land Cruiser was a single 1958 FJ25 sold through Rose Toyota. It's now at the Land Cruiser Heritage Museum. IH8MUD's FJ2X registry lists import figures of 61 Land Cruisers in 1959 and 162 in 1960.

faq.q: Is it really a FJ25 or a rebodied FJ40?
faq.a: Check the frame, not the plate. IH8MUD members point to the under-seat fuel tank, round rear wheel cut-outs, a flat floor without an offset transfer-case hump, a centered rear differential and FJ25-specific spring hangers and steering center link. A VIN plate on a later tub, or a 2F head on an F block, is a warning sign.

Engine and many service parts are shared with early F-engined FJ40s and still sold by specialists such as Cruiser Corps and Specter Off-Road. FJ25-specific chassis, body and hydraulic parts are another matter: Specter lists its FJ25 master-cylinder, clutch and distributor-cap items as discontinued, so owners trade among themselves through the IH8MUD FJ25 Owners Group.

faq.q: How do the brakes work, and are they safe?
faq.a: They're four-wheel drums with no booster. Each drum has two identical shoes, set with upper and lower cam adjusters. Kept adjusted, they stop like a 1950s truck should, which isn't well by modern standards. Some restored FJ25s sold on Bring a Trailer have front disc conversions.

Bring a Trailer FJ25 sales ran from $14,001 (2024) to $39,000 (2021), with a 2F-swapped 1959 at $14,250 in 2025 and a refurbished F-powered 1959 at $37,500 in 2026. CLASSIC.com shows 1957 FJ25s selling at Mecum and Barrett-Jackson for $33,000 in 2026. RM Sotheby's sold a restored 1960 soft-top for $70,000 in 2019.
faq.src: BRING A TRAILER · CLASSIC.COM · RM SOTHEBY'S

faq.q: Can I import one into the US?
faq.a: Yes. Every J20 is far older than the 25-year threshold for NHTSA's import exemption, and most FJ25s sold in the US recently came from Latin America. Allow for state titling and emissions rules (California is the hard one) and make sure the paperwork matches the frame number.

mods.why: Specter Off-Road is one of the few suppliers with an FJ25 section, from pedal pads and clutch slave boots to used bellhousings. Check its discontinued items before you strip anything you can't replace.
Gaskets, ignition parts, thermostats and fuel pumps listed from 1958 for F-engined Land Cruisers. They're catalogued for FJ40s, so confirm fit for a 25.
Old radiators are expensive to re-core. Owners report later OEM and Cool Cruisers of Texas radiators fitting FJ25s if originality isn't the priority.

Specter still lists standard and oversize flat-top F pistons and a valve regrind set for 1958-on Siamese-port F engines, which is what keeps original engines running instead of being replaced by a 2F.
For a full nut-and-bolt restoration, early-Land Cruiser specialists have the knowledge that a general shop won't have.

baseline_service.intro: Any FJ25 is now more than 65 years old, so assume nothing has been done and service everything. Toyota's capacities below are for the F engine as fitted to the 40 and 55 Series (compiled on IH8MUD from Toyota publications). The FJ25's own gearbox and transfer case aren't in that table, so check its figures in an FJ25 manual.

items.spec: F engine: 7 L, API SD in Toyota's table · canister (cartridge) filter element, Toyota 04152-60060
items.interval: Baseline now; then per the owner's manual
items.note: Early F engines use a canister filter, not a spin-on. An IH8MUD member says the dealer element comes with its gasket and washer. Use a modern oil suited to a flat-tappet engine.

items.spec: Short-reach plugs (Champion J8C / NGK B6S / ND W14-U per the IH8MUD FJ25 list) · points gap 0.018 in (Cruiser Corps, 1958–75 F)
items.note: Set timing with the octane adjuster after replacing points. Check that the moving-body vacuum advance works.
Same procedure as an early FJ40 F engine. New cork cover gasket.

items.spec: F engine: 15.2 L (Toyota's early table lists plain water; use ethylene-glycol coolant)
items.note: FJ25 hose part numbers on IH8MUD: upper 90916-01019, lower hoses 90916-01021, thermostat 90916-03014.

items.spec: Metal-bowl filter with element (Toyota 04234-30010 per the IH8MUD FJ25 list) · mechanical pump
items.note: Old fuel varnishes carburetors. Clean the bowl and blow out the lines before rebuilding the carb.

items.spec: Gear oil per FJ25 manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Toyota's 40-series table specifies API GL-4 SAE 90 for its gearboxes and transfer case)
items.note: The FJ25 has a single-speed transfer case and a different four-speed from the 40-series J30/H41, so don't borrow the 40-series capacities.

items.spec: Hypoid gear oil [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (Toyota's 40-series table: API GL-5 80W-90, 2.5 L)
items.note: The FJ25 has a centered rear differential. IH8MUD says its rear axle isn't the same as an FJ40's centered axle, so don't assume parts swap.
Two cast-iron master cylinders (brake and clutch). Look for weeping wheel cylinders on all four drums.

items.spec: Chassis: moly lithium NLGI-2 · wheel bearings: lithium multipurpose NLGI-2 (Toyota 40-series table)
items.interval: Grease now; repack wheel bearings now
items.note: The IH8MUD FJ25 list cross-references front inner bearings (Federal-Mogul 26820/26882), outer (BR2720/BR2788) and rear (Koyo R139B).

parts.name: Universal joints, FJ40/45 1958–73 (confirm FJ25 cap size)

items.spec: Fan belt, Toyota 90916-02008 (IH8MUD FJ25 list) · gear-driven camshaft, so no timing belt
items.note: The F engine drives its camshaft by gears. Toyota's 13523-60030 is listed as the steel replacement for the original fiber cam gear.
